title: MV Making an (actually fun) timing/rhythm-based parry mechanic

posts.author: Spacialrended
posts.body:
So; here's a predicament I've been having:
I don't like not being given the option to avoid attacks. One of my favorite things about games like Undertale, Deltarune, The Mario RPGs, etc. is the ability to Dodge attacks and be more in control of the battle instead of letting RNG decide.
I had been struggling to come up with a good dodge/parry mechanic for my game for awhile, until I thought up something really interesting:
"what if i made it like Taiko/Muse Dash/Unbeatable? A couple lanes and 2 main note types."
Spoiler:
A rough mockup of what i imagine Enemy is not depicted)
Basically, You have the 2 lanes, Regular notes, Hold notes, Bash notes (which means you have to mash both keys), Binded notes (Notes that require you to press both keys) and possibly heal notes for if you mess up and SP/MP up notes to heal SP. The charts for the battles would be done with a plugin I'd (probably) have to make myself that can read BPM and know how to change the track of the song from not defending to actively defending (My other idea was adaptive music)
So... i thought this would be a fun idea, right?
well, here's where today's overthinking-induced problem comes in:
To give an example of a game that could use this system, My game is planned to have a variety of battle songs, but I also, at the same time, am worried about how long it will take to MAKE all these songs and make the charts. (I personally would never rely on AI for those things, so let's keep that out of the conversation.)
Then there's the problems that apply to both me and someone who may be making a game with less music. (If I cut back on the battle songs for my game, this could apply to me too.)
What if people get BORED of the Songs and/or charts? There's only so many you can put in, and for a longer game it could get boring.
The only compromise I can think of is making it exclusive to bosses and minibosses, since those are important and thus usually have their own original songs.
Soooo... Do you guys have any better ideas? Am I overthinking the problems? Is this a fun concept? Am I just young and overambitious and need to go back to the drawing board?
Please let me know what you think.
Thanks, Derek "Spacialrended" Bunmore

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I'd ask myself first how I plan on executing this plan on a technical level before considering how to handle it on a creative level.
Not to sound like a certain festive cat that prowls the forum, but I'm not entirely sure RPG Maker is a viable route for handling this. Other engines would likely be more suited for this type of gameplay.
Of course, if you have a deep understanding of JS then Bob's your uncle, but without the pockets to pay someone to make this or the knowledge of knowing how you probably want to scale back the idea.

posts.author: LowrellLovelace
posts.body:
This concept sounds very fun and plenty of other games have also used this concept (look at every rhythm based battle game). In fact, there's already several plugins that make rhythm minigames :
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/tamfeys-timed-button-attacks.56684/
There's other plugins I'm just being lazy rn
But, there's only been three plugins that I would consider actually "of quality" to use that I've seen.
https://walkingdream.itch.io/rhythm-game-mz
<- Probably what you're looking for
https://store.steampowered.com/app/4099720/RPG_Maker_MV__Rhythm_Game_Maker/?snr=1_5_9__405
<- No downloads ;-;
But this story changes drastically if you want to make your OWN plugin or you can't afford 10$ like me. IMO this would be very VERY hard to implement with rpg maker. I wouldn't say I'm the best person to ask advice from as, self-admittedly, we know rhythm games are possible with plugins yet I couldn't even come close to implementing one. But, from what I know, you would encounter at least 2 large problems making a music rhythm based game with rpg maker.
RPG maker mz and mv runs on their own game time, 60 frames per second. Which means whatever music charts you have on screen could become off-sync with the AudioManager which runs independently from the game logic when the music is playing which is especially bad if you're planning to make a beat map several minutes long and on repeat. I've came up with a solution to this with my plugin:
MusicEventTimers
, by setting a timestamp in the BGM and having an alarm activate at that point. But it's very rough and buggy and I would suggest you just look at my code and Frankenstein it to a beat map if you're serious about this.
Javascript, what rpg maker runs on, is single threaded, which means that it can only run code line one by one. Most rhythm games are programmed on c# or other multithreaded languages (correct me if I'm wrong). So the best way to try to implement audio tracking would to multithread a process that runs independently from the game logic, so it be less slowed down by any potential lag or issues. But the closest thing in Javascript to multithreading are web workers, promises, and probably some other stuff I'm not aware of. The problem here is that any documented help around that stuff specifically on rpg maker is bare bones and no one actually talks about how to implement it code-wise.
Here's the resources I found that might help you:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/multithread-on-mz.147545/
https://developer.mozilla.org/enUS/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API/Using_web_workers
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aAc7Ia6gPM
https://github.com/thinknathan/mv-multithreaded-save
https://nodejs.org/api/worker_threads.html
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/for-mz-howto-get-data-out-of-a-promise-solved-with-using-async-twice-and-await-twice.157958/
Again I'm not the best person to ask but I'm just here to give my two cents on the matter.
As for the actual implementation of battle songs. I would say to go for quality over quantity. It's better to have one memorable song than multiple flops. And I would also suggest to not even attempt something this big if you're not passionate about music making. Passion is something easily sensed by players and they will know if you skimped out on something. Plus, you should study on music theory and the structure and melodies on songs you do like. It's not necessary but it will marginally make up for any lack of experience you may have.

posts.author: LowrellLovelace
Spacialrended
NamEtag
posts.body:
RPGs generally have bosses with high hp and no healing, while players have fairly low max hp but tons of healing. Sometimes it's so abysmally low that you need dedicated hp gear just to take 1 hit, and sometimes healing sucks. This is highly incompatible with skill-based damage mitigation.
You create 2 hard issues when combining these together: 1 is a hard skill requirement for how
consistently
successful a player has to be to even be worthy of surviving more than 1 round. The other is a direct and exponential difference in turn economy between perfect play and bad play. If you need to spend nearly all your actions every round healing the damage you take, then you'll take 20 times longer than someone who completely ignores healing and parries everything.
At least when used as bonus damage on bosses, it's easier to avoid softlocks. There's a guaranteed minimum damage, and there won't be completely useless rounds.
What I recommend is generating resources that changes depending on the song, and only playing short segments of the chart that depends on
when
the minigame was activated in the song. And these resources could potentially be used by the enemy as well.
